    After Diversity Maximum Demand Calculator¶

    The admdspenmw package estimates the After Diversity Maximum Demand (ADMD) of a group of homes on a feeder - the peak demand the group places on the network once the fact that individual peaks do not coincide is allowed for. It is a Python version of the Public ADMD Calculator V1.1 spreadsheet of SP Energy Networks (SP Manweb), extended with electric vehicle chargers, heat pumps and storage heating. The app uses it in the postprocessing of Sprake consumption results (calculate_sprake_admd) to estimate the ADMD of a site.

    There are two results: ADMD_standard for standard (peak) conditions, and ADMD_coldload for cold load pickup - the demand when supply is restored after an interruption and heating loads run together.

    Method¶

    For a number of customers, the calculator chooses a diversity level (1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 50, 100 customers - the more customers, the more diversity). For each group of households - those with an EV charger, each type and size of heat pump, storage heating, or no low carbon technology (LCT) - a tabulated per-household demand at that level (src/admdspenmw/data/admd_lookups.csv, from the spreadsheet) is multiplied by the number of households in the group. The groups are summed, and a correction is subtracted for households with both an EV charger and a heat pump, which were counted in both groups.

    flowchart TB
    N["N_customers"] --> DL["diversity_level"]
    DL --> EV["EV_total<br/>(EV_NSC, EV_SC)"]
    DL --> HP["ASHP / GSHP / HyHP<br/>5, 8, 16 kW<br/>standard and coldload"]
    DL --> ST["storage 5, 8, 16 kW"]
    DL --> NL["no_lct_standard_total"]
    NEV["N_EV_chargers<br/>N_EV_and_HP<br/>N_..._kW counts"] --> EV
    NEV --> HP
    NEV --> ST
    NEV --> NNL["N_no_lct"] --> NL
    EV --> SUB["admd_standard_subtotal_1<br/>admd_coldload_subtotal_1"]
    HP --> TOT["type totals"] --> SUB
    ST --> SUB
    NL --> SUB
    SUB --> ADMD["ADMD_standard<br/>ADMD_coldload"]
    DL --> ADMD
    NEV --> ADMD

    The functions of admdspenmw.admd are the nodes of a Hamilton dataflow: each function is named for the value it calculates and takes the values it depends on as parameters. The inputs are the numbers of customers, EV chargers and systems of each size. newsegsmodelframework.util.admd_helpers builds the driver, and model_config holds the defaults.

    Sizing systems from dwellings¶

    Systems are sized by dwelling in the NewSEGS software (ASHP_count and its siblings): apartments and homes of fewer than 3 bedrooms use 5 kW, 3-4 bedrooms 8 kW and 5 or more bedrooms 16 kW. This follows the spreadsheet's Assumptions sheet.

    Differences from the spreadsheet¶

    • The battery storage reduction (40% of peak if the battery is at least three times the ADMD in kWh) is not implemented; the spreadsheet's calculation of it refers to a missing cell.
    • The spreadsheet's three input columns (bedroom bands, each with one average system size) are replaced by counts of systems per size.
    • More than 101 customers use diversity level 200 (values equal to level 100), where the spreadsheet gives N/A.
    • Results are totals for the feeder, not an average per household.

    The full list of assumptions and the functions are documented below.

    diversity_level(N_customers) ¶

    Diversity level for a number of customers on the feeder.

    The ADMD of a group of customers falls, per customer, as the group gets larger, because their peak demands do not coincide. The calculator therefore tabulates demand for a set of diversity levels (the number of customers the tabulated value is for), and the level to use is chosen from the number of customers:

    Customers Diversity level
    1 - 4 1
    5 - 9 5
    10 - 14 10
    15 - 19 15
    20 - 24 20
    25 - 49 25
    50 - 80 50
    81 - 101 100
    102 or more 200

    This is the "Establish Diversity Level" row of the spreadsheet. The spreadsheet gives N/A for more than 101 customers; here level 200 is used instead, which has the same values as level 100 in admd_lookups.csv.

    def diversity_level(N_customers:int) -> int:
    """Diversity level for a number of customers on the feeder.

    The ADMD of a group of customers falls, per customer, as the group gets larger, because
    their peak demands do not coincide. The calculator therefore tabulates demand for a
    set of *diversity levels* (the number of customers the tabulated value is for), and the
    level to use is chosen from the number of customers:

    | Customers | Diversity level |
    |---|---|
    | 1 - 4 | 1 |
    | 5 - 9 | 5 |
    | 10 - 14 | 10 |
    | 15 - 19 | 15 |
    | 20 - 24 | 20 |
    | 25 - 49 | 25 |
    | 50 - 80 | 50 |
    | 81 - 101 | 100 |
    | 102 or more | 200 |

    This is the "Establish Diversity Level" row of the spreadsheet. The spreadsheet gives
    `N/A` for more than 101 customers; here level 200 is used instead, which has the same
    values as level 100 in `admd_lookups.csv`.

    Args:
        N_customers: Number of customers (households) on the feeder.

    Returns:
        The diversity level; the index of the lookup table.
    """
    match 1:
        case 1 if (N_customers < 5):
            return 1
        case 1 if (N_customers < 10):
            return 5
        case 1 if (N_customers < 15):
            return 10
        case 1 if (N_customers < 20):
            return 15
        case 1 if (N_customers < 25):
            return 20
        case 1 if (N_customers < 50):
            return 25
        case 1 if (N_customers < 81):
            return 50
        case 1 if (N_customers < 102):
            return 100
        case _:
            return 200

    def EV_NSC(diversity_level:int,
           N_EV_chargers:float
           ) -> float:
    """ADMD of the electric vehicle chargers with no smart charging (standard conditions).

    Per-household demand for a household with a 7.36 kW (or two 3.68 kW) charger without
    smart charging, at the diversity level, multiplied by the number of chargers. The per-unit
    value includes the base household demand.
    Spreadsheet row: "Calculate Non Smart Charge Value".

    Args:
        diversity_level: Diversity level, from `diversity_level`.
        N_EV_chargers: Number of households with an EV charger.

    Returns:
        ADMD in kW of the households with EV chargers.
    """
    return lookups.loc[diversity_level,'EV_NSC_standard_perunit'] * N_EV_chargers

    def EV_total(EV_NSC:float,
             EV_SC:float,
             smart_charging:bool
             ) -> float:
    """ADMD of the electric vehicle chargers, with or without smart charging.

    Selects `EV_SC` if smart charging is present, otherwise `EV_NSC`. The same value is used
    for the standard and cold load pickup calculations.
    Spreadsheet row: "Calculate EV Total".

    Args:
        EV_NSC: ADMD with no smart charging, from `EV_NSC`.
        EV_SC: ADMD with smart charging, from `EV_SC`.
        smart_charging: Whether the chargers have smart charging.

    Returns:
        ADMD in kW of the households with EV chargers.
    """
    if smart_charging:
        return EV_SC
    else:
        return EV_NSC

    ASHP_5kW_standard(diversity_level, N_ASHP_5kW) ¶

    ADMD of the households with a 5 kW ASHP under standard (peak) conditions.

    The per-household demand at the diversity level (column ASHP_5kW_standard_perunit of admd_lookups.csv) multiplied by the number of households. The 5 kW size is for a 1-2 bedroom house, with insulation to 1990s standard or better; the heating system is an air source heat pump (ASHP) with a 5 kW heat output which provides space heating and hot water and includes a direct electric backup heater. Its undiversified demand is 2.41 kW electrical. The per- household value includes the base household demand. Spreadsheet row: "Calculate 5kW ASHP Total".

    def ASHP_8kW_standard(diversity_level:int,
                      N_ASHP_8kW:float
                      ) -> float:
    """ADMD of the households with a 8 kW ASHP under standard (peak) conditions.

    The per-household demand at the diversity level (column `ASHP_8kW_standard_perunit` of
    `admd_lookups.csv`) multiplied by the number of households. The 8 kW size is for a 3-4
    bedroom house, with insulation to 1990s standard or better; the heating system is an
    air source heat pump (ASHP) with a 8 kW heat output which provides space heating and
    hot water and includes a direct electric backup heater. Its undiversified demand is
    4.68 kW electrical. The per- household value includes the base household demand.
    Spreadsheet row: "Calculate 8kW ASHP Total".

    Args:
        diversity_level: Diversity level, from `diversity_level`.
        N_ASHP_8kW: Number of households with this system.

    Returns:
        ADMD in kW of those households (a total, not a value per household).
    """
    return lookups.loc[diversity_level,'ASHP_8kW_standard_perunit'] * N_ASHP_8kW

    def storage_8kW_standard(diversity_level:int,
                         N_storage_8kW:float
                         ) -> float:
    """ADMD of the households with a 8 kW storage heating system under standard (peak) conditions.

    The per-household demand at the diversity level (column `storage_8kW_standard_perunit`
    of `admd_lookups.csv`) multiplied by the number of households. The 8 kW size is for a
    3-4 bedroom house, with insulation to 1990s standard or better; the heating system is
    an electric storage heating system with a 8 kW electrical rating which provides space
    heating only. Its undiversified demand is 8 kW. The per-household value includes the
    base household demand. Spreadsheet row: "Calculate 8kW Storage Total".

    The spreadsheet has no separate cold load pickup values for storage heating, so there
    is no `storage_*_coldload` function: `storage_standard_total` is used in
    `admd_coldload_subtotal_1` too.

        N_storage_8kW: Number of households with this system.

    Returns:
        ADMD in kW of those households (a total, not a value per household).
    """
    return lookups.loc[diversity_level,'storage_8kW_standard_perunit'] * N_storage_8kW

    def N_no_lct(N_customers:int,
             N_EV_chargers:float,
             N_EV_and_HP:float,
             N_ASHP:float,
             N_GSHP:float,
             N_HyHP:float,
             N_storage:float
             ) -> float:
    """Number of standalone households, with no low carbon technology (LCT).

    The customers on the feeder, less those that have an EV charger without a heat pump
    (`N_EV_chargers - N_EV_and_HP`), and those with an ASHP, GSHP, hybrid heat pump or storage
    heating. Households with both an EV charger and a heat pump are removed with the heat
    pump households, so they are not removed twice. This is the quantity used in the spreadsheet
    row "Calculate Standalone Households Total (No LCTs)".

    Args:
        N_customers: Number of customers on the feeder.
        N_EV_chargers: Number of households with an EV charger.
        N_EV_and_HP: Number of households with both an EV charger and a heat pump.
        N_ASHP: Number of households with an ASHP, from `N_ASHP`.
        N_GSHP: Number of households with a GSHP, from `N_GSHP`.
        N_HyHP: Number of households with a hybrid heat pump, from `N_HyHP`.
        N_storage: Number of households with storage heating, from `N_storage`.

    Returns:
        Number of households with no LCT.
    """
    return N_customers - (N_EV_chargers - N_EV_and_HP) - N_ASHP - N_GSHP - N_HyHP - N_storage

    ADMD_standard(diversity_level, admd_standard_subtotal_1, N_EV_and_HP) ¶

    After Diversity Maximum Demand of the feeder under standard conditions.

    The subtotal less a correction of ev_hp_cofactor (from admd_lookups.csv) for each household that has both an EV charger and a heat pump. Each of those households has been counted in both the EV and the heat pump totals, and each total includes the base household demand, so one base household demand is removed. The cofactor is 1.1 kW for 20 or more customers (diversity levels 20 to 200), and the house-only demand for fewer. Spreadsheet rows: "Reduce load by required level Sub Total 2" and "Total ADMD".

    The result is the total for all customers; divide by the number of customers for the "Average kW ADMD Per House Hold".

    Note

    The spreadsheet has a further row, "Calculate Battery ADMD Reduction Effect", which would reduce ADMD by 40% of the peak where there is sufficient battery capacity (at least three times the ADMD without a battery, in kWh). It refers to a missing cell (#REF!) in the spreadsheet, is not used in its total, and is not implemented here.

    The subtotal less a correction of `ev_hp_cofactor` (from `admd_lookups.csv`) for each
    household that has both an EV charger and a heat pump. Each of those households has been
    counted in both the EV and the heat pump totals, and each total includes the base
    household demand, so one base household demand is removed. The cofactor is 1.1 kW for 20
    or more customers (diversity levels 20 to 200), and the house-only demand for fewer.
    Spreadsheet rows: "Reduce load by required level Sub Total 2" and "Total ADMD".

    The result is the total for all customers; divide by the number of customers for the
    "Average kW ADMD Per House Hold".

    Note:
        The spreadsheet has a further row, "Calculate Battery ADMD Reduction Effect", which would
        reduce ADMD by 40% of the peak where there is sufficient battery capacity (at least three
        times the ADMD without a battery, in kWh). It refers to a missing cell (`#REF!`) in the
        spreadsheet, is not used in its total, and is not implemented here.

    Args:
        diversity_level: Diversity level, from `diversity_level`.
        admd_standard_subtotal_1: Subtotal, from `admd_standard_subtotal_1`.
        N_EV_and_HP: Number of households with both an EV charger and a heat pump.

    Returns:
        ADMD in kW of all customers on the feeder.
    """
    return (
        admd_standard_subtotal_1
            - N_EV_and_HP * lookups.loc[diversity_level,'ev_hp_cofactor']
    )

    After Diversity Maximum Demand of the feeder under cold load pickup conditions.

    Cold load pickup is the demand when supply is restored after an interruption, when thermostatically controlled heating loads are running simultaneously. The result is the subtotal less a correction for households with both an EV charger and a heat pump, as in ADMD_standard, but using ev_hp_coldload_cofactor (the house-only demand at the diversity level). 1030
1031
    def ADMD_coldload(diversity_level:int,
                  admd_coldload_subtotal_1:float,
                  N_EV_and_HP:float
                  ) -> float:
    """After Diversity Maximum Demand of the feeder under cold load pickup conditions.

    Cold load pickup is the demand when supply is restored after an interruption, when
    thermostatically controlled heating loads are running simultaneously. The result is the
    subtotal less a correction for households with both an EV charger and a heat pump, as in
    `ADMD_standard`, but using `ev_hp_coldload_cofactor` (the house-only demand at the diversity
    level). Spreadsheet column: "Cold Load Pickup".

    Args:
        diversity_level: Diversity level, from `diversity_level`.
        admd_coldload_subtotal_1: Subtotal, from `admd_coldload_subtotal_1`.
        N_EV_and_HP: Number of households with both an EV charger and a heat pump.

    Returns:
        ADMD in kW of all customers on the feeder.
    """
    return (
        admd_coldload_subtotal_1
            - N_EV_and_HP * lookups.loc[diversity_level,'ev_hp_coldload_cofactor']
    )

    def ASHP_count(type_:np.ndarray[tuple[int], np.dtype[str]],
               beds:np.ndarray[tuple[int], np.dtype[int]]
               ) -> dict:
    """Count of air source heat pump systems by size for a set of dwellings, assuming one per dwelling.

    Sizes the system by dwelling, following the sizing of the calculator's assumptions:
    apartments and houses with fewer than 3 bedrooms get 5 kW; houses with 3 or 4 bedrooms
    get 8 kW; houses with 5 or more bedrooms get 16 kW. (The spreadsheet instead takes a
    number of systems and one average size for each of three bedroom bands. Treating
    apartments as 5 kW is an assumption of this function.) The result provides the
    `N_ASHP_*kW` inputs of the calculation. `ASHP_count`, `GSHP_count`, `HyHP_count` and
    `storage_count` all use the same rule.

    Args:
        type_: Array of dwelling types; `'apt'` for an apartment, anything else is a house.
        beds: Array of number of bedrooms of the dwellings.

    Returns:
        Dict of `N_ASHP_5kW`, `N_ASHP_8kW` and `N_ASHP_16kW` - the number of
        dwellings in each size band.
    """
    is_apt = type_ == 'apt'
    is_5kW = np.logical_or(
        is_apt,
        beds < 3
    )
    is_8kW = np.logical_and(
        np.logical_not(is_apt),
        np.logical_and(
            beds >= 3,
            beds < 5
        )
    )
    is_16kW = np.logical_and(
        np.logical_not(is_apt),
        beds >= 5
    )
    return {
        'N_ASHP_5kW': float(np.sum(is_5kW)),
        'N_ASHP_8kW': float(np.sum(is_8kW)),
        'N_ASHP_16kW': float(np.sum(is_16kW))
    }

    admd ¶

    After Diversity Maximum Demand (ADMD) calculation for housing with low carbon technologies.

    A Python version of the Public ADMD Calculator V1.1 spreadsheet published by SP Energy Networks for the SP Manweb area (the spenmw of the package name); see the calculator. It estimates the maximum demand, in kW, that a group of customers on a feeder places on the network after allowing for diversity - the fact that individual peaks do not coincide - when some households have electric vehicle (EV) chargers, heat pumps or storage heating.

    Two results are produced:

    • ADMD_standard - under standard (peak) conditions;
    • ADMD_coldload - under cold load pickup conditions, when supply is restored after an interruption and heating loads run simultaneously.
    Structure¶

    The functions form a dataflow graph for Hamilton: the name of each function is the name of the value it calculates, and its parameters are the names of the values it depends on - either other functions of this module, or inputs (N_customers, N_EV_chargers, N_EV_and_HP, smart_charging and the N_<type>_<size>kW counts of heat pumps and storage heating; see model_config.default_model_inputs). A Hamilton driver (see newsegsmodelframework.util.admd_helpers) executes only what is needed for the outputs requested. The calculation proceeds:

    1. diversity_level - from the number of customers.
    2. Per-group ADMD - EV_total (from EV_NSC or EV_SC); <type>_<size>kW_standard and <type>_<size>kW_coldload for ASHP, GSHP and HyHP; storage_<size>kW_standard; no_lct_standard_total for households with no low carbon technology (LCT), whose number is N_no_lct. Each is a per-household value from data/admd_lookups.csv at the diversity level, multiplied by a number of households.
    3. Totals per type - <type>_standard_total, <type>_coldload_total.
    4. admd_standard_subtotal_1 and admd_coldload_subtotal_1 - sums of the groups.
    5. ADMD_standard and ADMD_coldload - the subtotals less a correction for households counted twice because they have both an EV charger and a heat pump.

    ASHP_count, GSHP_count, HyHP_count and storage_count are helpers (not nodes of the graph) that size systems from the types and bedrooms of dwellings.

    Assumptions¶

    From the calculator's Assumptions sheet:

    • Sizes: 5 kW is for a 1-2 bedroom house, 8 kW for a 3-4 bedroom house and 16 kW for a 5+ bedroom house, with insulation to 1990s standard or better.
    • Domestic EV charge points are 7.36 kW; smart charging (a control that reduces EV charging during peak hours) is modelled as 3.68 kW.
    • ASHPs provide space heating and hot water and include a direct electric backup heater. GSHPs and hybrid heat pumps have no backup heater. Hybrid heat pumps are bi-valent, switching to gas below 8 °C. Storage heating provides space heating only.
    • A standalone household with no LCT has an ADMD of about 2 kW (1.8 kW in the tables at 100 customers).

    Undiversified electrical load of each system (kW), standard / cold load pickup:

    System 5 kW 8 kW 16 kW
    ASHP 2.41 / 3.38 4.68 / 6.55 9.37 / 13.12
    GSHP 2.6 3.8 6.5
    Hybrid 1.22 2.69 4.57
    Storage heating 5 8 16
    Differences from the spreadsheet¶
    • The battery storage reduction of the spreadsheet is not implemented (it refers to a missing cell in V1.1).
    • The spreadsheet's three input columns (bedroom bands, each with one average heat pump size) and its combination of the three using a "Total Diversity Level" are replaced by counts of systems by size; see ASHP_count.
    • More than 101 customers use diversity level 200, rather than N/A.
    • The ADMD_* results are totals for the feeder, not an average per household.
    • At diversity level 20 the spreadsheet's house-only table gives 2.4 kW but its standalone household formula uses 2.2 kW; the lookup table here uses 2.2 kW for standalone households.

    diversity_level(N_customers) ¶

    Diversity level for a number of customers on the feeder.

    The ADMD of a group of customers falls, per customer, as the group gets larger, because their peak demands do not coincide. The calculator therefore tabulates demand for a set of diversity levels (the number of customers the tabulated value is for), and the level to use is chosen from the number of customers:

    Customers Diversity level
    1 - 4 1
    5 - 9 5
    10 - 14 10
    15 - 19 15
    20 - 24 20
    25 - 49 25
    50 - 80 50
    81 - 101 100
    102 or more 200

    This is the "Establish Diversity Level" row of the spreadsheet. The spreadsheet gives N/A for more than 101 customers; here level 200 is used instead, which has the same values as level 100 in admd_lookups.csv.

    def diversity_level(N_customers:int) -> int:
    """Diversity level for a number of customers on the feeder.

    The ADMD of a group of customers falls, per customer, as the group gets larger, because
    their peak demands do not coincide. The calculator therefore tabulates demand for a
    set of *diversity levels* (the number of customers the tabulated value is for), and the
    level to use is chosen from the number of customers:

    | Customers | Diversity level |
    |---|---|
    | 1 - 4 | 1 |
    | 5 - 9 | 5 |
    | 10 - 14 | 10 |
    | 15 - 19 | 15 |
    | 20 - 24 | 20 |
    | 25 - 49 | 25 |
    | 50 - 80 | 50 |
    | 81 - 101 | 100 |
    | 102 or more | 200 |

    This is the "Establish Diversity Level" row of the spreadsheet. The spreadsheet gives
    `N/A` for more than 101 customers; here level 200 is used instead, which has the same
    values as level 100 in `admd_lookups.csv`.

    Args:
        N_customers: Number of customers (households) on the feeder.

    Returns:
        The diversity level; the index of the lookup table.
    """
    match 1:
        case 1 if (N_customers < 5):
            return 1
        case 1 if (N_customers < 10):
            return 5
        case 1 if (N_customers < 15):
            return 10
        case 1 if (N_customers < 20):
            return 15
        case 1 if (N_customers < 25):
            return 20
        case 1 if (N_customers < 50):
            return 25
        case 1 if (N_customers < 81):
            return 50
        case 1 if (N_customers < 102):
            return 100
        case _:
            return 200

    def EV_total(EV_NSC:float,
             EV_SC:float,
             smart_charging:bool
             ) -> float:
    """ADMD of the electric vehicle chargers, with or without smart charging.

    Selects `EV_SC` if smart charging is present, otherwise `EV_NSC`. The same value is used
    for the standard and cold load pickup calculations.
    Spreadsheet row: "Calculate EV Total".

    Args:
        EV_NSC: ADMD with no smart charging, from `EV_NSC`.
        EV_SC: ADMD with smart charging, from `EV_SC`.
        smart_charging: Whether the chargers have smart charging.

    Returns:
        ADMD in kW of the households with EV chargers.
    """
    if smart_charging:
        return EV_SC
    else:
        return EV_NSC

    ASHP_5kW_standard(diversity_level, N_ASHP_5kW) ¶

    ADMD of the households with a 5 kW ASHP under standard (peak) conditions.

    HyHP_16kW_standard(diversity_level, N_HyHP_16kW) ¶

    The per-household demand at the diversity level (column HyHP_16kW_standard_perunit of admd_lookups.csv) multiplied by the number of households. The 16 kW size is for a 5+ bedroom house, with insulation to 1990s standard or better; the heating system is an hybrid heat pump with a 16 kW heat output which provides space heating and hot water, has no backup heater and is bi-valent: it switches to gas when the outside temperature falls below a threshold (8 °C in the spreadsheet).     def N_no_lct(N_customers:int,
             N_EV_chargers:float,
             N_EV_and_HP:float,
             N_ASHP:float,
             N_GSHP:float,
             N_HyHP:float,
             N_storage:float
             ) -> float:
    """Number of standalone households, with no low carbon technology (LCT).

    The customers on the feeder, less those that have an EV charger without a heat pump
    (`N_EV_chargers - N_EV_and_HP`), and those with an ASHP, GSHP, hybrid heat pump or storage
    heating. Households with both an EV charger and a heat pump are removed with the heat
    pump households, so they are not removed twice. This is the quantity used in the spreadsheet
    row "Calculate Standalone Households Total (No LCTs)".

    Args:
        N_customers: Number of customers on the feeder.
        N_EV_chargers: Number of households with an EV charger.
        N_EV_and_HP: Number of households with both an EV charger and a heat pump.
        N_ASHP: Number of households with an ASHP, from `N_ASHP`.
        N_GSHP: Number of households with a GSHP, from `N_GSHP`.
        N_HyHP: Number of households with a hybrid heat pump, from `N_HyHP`.
        N_storage: Number of households with storage heating, from `N_storage`.

    Returns:
        Number of households with no LCT.
    """
    return N_customers - (N_EV_chargers - N_EV_and_HP) - N_ASHP - N_GSHP - N_HyHP - N_storage

        EV_total: ADMD of households with EV chargers, from `EV_total`.
        ASHP_standard_total: from `ASHP_standard_total`.
        GSHP_standard_total: from `GSHP_standard_total`.
        HyHP_standard_total: from `HyHP_standard_total`.
        storage_standard_total: from `storage_standard_total`.
        no_lct_standard_total: from `no_lct_standard_total`.

    Returns:
        ADMD in kW, before correction.
    """
    return EV_total + ASHP_standard_total + GSHP_standard_total + HyHP_standard_total + storage_standard_total + no_lct_standard_total

    ADMD_standard(diversity_level, admd_standard_subtotal_1, N_EV_and_HP) ¶

    After Diversity Maximum Demand of the feeder under standard conditions.

    The subtotal less a correction of ev_hp_cofactor (from admd_lookups.csv) for each household that has both an EV charger and a heat pump. Each of those households has been counted in both the EV and the heat pump totals, and each total includes the base household demand, so one base household demand is removed. The cofactor is 1.1 kW for 20 or more customers (diversity levels 20 to 200), and the house-only demand for fewer. Spreadsheet rows: "Reduce load by required level Sub Total 2" and "Total ADMD".

    The result is the total for all customers; divide by the number of customers for the "Average kW ADMD Per House Hold".

    Note

    The spreadsheet has a further row, "Calculate Battery ADMD Reduction Effect", which would reduce ADMD by 40% of the peak where there is sufficient battery capacity (at least three times the ADMD without a battery, in kWh). It refers to a missing cell (#REF!) in the spreadsheet, is not used in its total, and is not implemented here.

    def ADMD_standard(diversity_level:int,
                  admd_standard_subtotal_1:float,
                  N_EV_and_HP:float
                  ) -> float:
    """After Diversity Maximum Demand of the feeder under standard conditions.

    The subtotal less a correction of `ev_hp_cofactor` (from `admd_lookups.csv`) for each
    household that has both an EV charger and a heat pump. Each of those households has been
    counted in both the EV and the heat pump totals, and each total includes the base
    household demand, so one base household demand is removed. The cofactor is 1.1 kW for 20
    or more customers (diversity levels 20 to 200), and the house-only demand for fewer.
    Spreadsheet rows: "Reduce load by required level Sub Total 2" and "Total ADMD".

    The result is the total for all customers; divide by the number of customers for the
    "Average kW ADMD Per House Hold".

    Note:
        The spreadsheet has a further row, "Calculate Battery ADMD Reduction Effect", which would
        reduce ADMD by 40% of the peak where there is sufficient battery capacity (at least three
        times the ADMD without a battery, in kWh). It refers to a missing cell (`#REF!`) in the
        spreadsheet, is not used in its total, and is not implemented here.

    Args:
        diversity_level: Diversity level, from `diversity_level`.
        admd_standard_subtotal_1: Subtotal, from `admd_standard_subtotal_1`.
        N_EV_and_HP: Number of households with both an EV charger and a heat pump.

    Returns:
        ADMD in kW of all customers on the feeder.
    """
    return (
        admd_standard_subtotal_1
            - N_EV_and_HP * lookups.loc[diversity_level,'ev_hp_cofactor']
    )

    HyHP_16kW_coldload(diversity_level, N_HyHP_16kW) ¶

    ADMD of the households with a 16 kW HyHP under cold load pickup conditions.

    The per-household demand at the diversity level (column HyHP_16kW_coldload_perunit of admd_lookups.csv) multiplied by the number of households. The 16 kW size is for a 5+ bedroom house, with insulation to 1990s standard or better; the heating system is an hybrid heat pump with a 16 kW heat output which provides space heating and hot water, has no backup heater and is bi-valent: it switches to gas when the outside temperature falls below a threshold (8 °C in the spreadsheet).     def ADMD_coldload(diversity_level:int,
                  admd_coldload_subtotal_1:float,
                  N_EV_and_HP:float
                  ) -> float:
    """After Diversity Maximum Demand of the feeder under cold load pickup conditions.

    Cold load pickup is the demand when supply is restored after an interruption, when
    thermostatically controlled heating loads are running simultaneously. The result is the
    subtotal less a correction for households with both an EV charger and a heat pump, as in
    `ADMD_standard`, but using `ev_hp_coldload_cofactor` (the house-only demand at the diversity
    level). Spreadsheet column: "Cold Load Pickup".

    Args:
        diversity_level: Diversity level, from `diversity_level`.
        admd_coldload_subtotal_1: Subtotal, from `admd_coldload_subtotal_1`.
        N_EV_and_HP: Number of households with both an EV charger and a heat pump.

    Returns:
        ADMD in kW of all customers on the feeder.
    """
    return (
        admd_coldload_subtotal_1
            - N_EV_and_HP * lookups.loc[diversity_level,'ev_hp_coldload_cofactor']
    )

    ASHP_count(type_, beds) ¶

    Count of air source heat pump systems by size for a set of dwellings, assuming one per dwelling.

    Sizes the system by dwelling, following the sizing of the calculator's assumptions: apartments and houses with fewer than 3 bedrooms get 5 kW; houses with 3 or 4 bedrooms get 8 kW; houses with 5 or more bedrooms get 16 kW. (The spreadsheet instead takes a number of systems and one average size for each of three bedroom bands. Treating apartments as 5 kW is an assumption of this function.) The result provides the N_ASHP_*kW inputs of the calculation. ASHP_count, GSHP_count, HyHP_count and storage_count all use the same rule.

    def ASHP_count(type_:np.ndarray[tuple[int], np.dtype[str]],
               beds:np.ndarray[tuple[int], np.dtype[int]]
               ) -> dict:
    """Count of air source heat pump systems by size for a set of dwellings, assuming one per dwelling.

    Sizes the system by dwelling, following the sizing of the calculator's assumptions:
    apartments and houses with fewer than 3 bedrooms get 5 kW; houses with 3 or 4 bedrooms
    get 8 kW; houses with 5 or more bedrooms get 16 kW. (The spreadsheet instead takes a
    number of systems and one average size for each of three bedroom bands. Treating
    apartments as 5 kW is an assumption of this function.) The result provides the
    `N_ASHP_*kW` inputs of the calculation. `ASHP_count`, `GSHP_count`, `HyHP_count` and
    `storage_count` all use the same rule.

    Args:
        type_: Array of dwelling types; `'apt'` for an apartment, anything else is a house.
        beds: Array of number of bedrooms of the dwellings.

    Returns:
        Dict of `N_ASHP_5kW`, `N_ASHP_8kW` and `N_ASHP_16kW` - the number of
        dwellings in each size band.
    """
    is_apt = type_ == 'apt'
    is_5kW = np.logical_or(
        is_apt,
        beds < 3
    )
    is_8kW = np.logical_and(
        np.logical_not(is_apt),
        np.logical_and(
            beds >= 3,
            beds < 5
        )
    )
    is_16kW = np.logical_and(
        np.logical_not(is_apt),
        beds >= 5
    )
    return {
        'N_ASHP_5kW': float(np.sum(is_5kW)),
        'N_ASHP_8kW': float(np.sum(is_8kW)),
        'N_ASHP_16kW': float(np.sum(is_16kW))
    }
